_comment: Canonical taxonomy for the RevisorPlus question bank. Single source of truth: validate_questions.py enforces it, `manage.py sync_taxonomy` writes it to the database, and elevenplus_data/CLAUDE.md documents it. Edit this file to change the taxonomy; do not hand-edit the copies. The `topic` layer is STRUCTURAL ONLY - it exists for navigation and for rolling up a pupil's weakness report, not as a claim about how real exams are organised. v2/v3 applied the seven-paper Maths audit (250 questions, 4 boards): see the `evidence` field on the MAT types. v4 adds the confirmed English and Verbal Reasoning taxonomies. Every ENG and VR question type carries `provenance`: 'authored' means the type is evidenced by a question already written (cited in `evidence`); 'proposed' means it is structurally expected but not yet confirmed against a real paper, and is the backlog for an English/VR paper audit of the kind the Maths rebuild ran. Subtopics in these two sections also carry a `slug` - the snake_case identifier authors write in packs - alongside the Title Case `name` used for display.

subtopics.name: Powers, Squares & Cubes
subtopics.target_rationale: absent from ISEB and Collins GL 9-10

subtopics.name: Four Operations

question_types.name: Column addition and subtraction
question_types.evidence: 3 papers, 2 boards: ISEB Q6; Collins GL 9-10 T3 Q9 (decimal column subtraction); Exam Coach GL Q14. The subtopic held only x, / and BIDMAS.

subtopics.target_rationale: gains addition-subtraction; auditors found papers lean heavily on plain arithmetic

question_types.name: Fraction of an amount
question_types.evidence: 3 papers + the project's own paper: Bond Q18/Q36 and Exam Coach GL Q11/Q34 were forced into multiplying-fractions; Collins CEM T3 Q4. percentage-of-amount had no fraction mirror.

question_types.name: One quantity as a fraction of another
question_types.evidence: 2 papers: Collins CEM T1 Q3; Bond Q39. The inverse of fraction-of-amount.

question_types.name: Converting between fractions, decimals and percentages
Ordering and comparing across forms
question_types.evidence: 1 paper + the project's own paper (fdp.ordering): Bond Q14 (decimals) and Q23 (fractions). Distinct from converting between forms.

subtopics.name: Statistics & Data

question_types.name: Read a single value
question_types.evidence: Split out in v3: the commonest statistics task in the audited papers was reading one value off a representation, which no existing type named - it was absorbed into whichever chart type was involved.

question_types.name: Compare two or more values
question_types.evidence: Split out in v3: 'how many MORE children chose apples than oranges' is a comparison performed ON a representation, not a property of bar charts. Collins GL 10-11 T1 Q7/Q8, Exam Coach GL.

question_types.name: A part as a proportion of the whole
question_types.evidence: Split out in v3: pie-chart angles and 'what fraction chose football' are one operation applied to several representations.

question_types.name: Tables and timetables
question_types.evidence: 5 papers - the most-confirmed gap in the audit: ISEB Q43 (frequency table); Collins CEM (bus timetable); Collins GL 9-10 (5 data tables); Collins GL 10-11 (3); Exam Coach GL (2).

question_types.name: Pictograms with a symbol key
question_types.evidence: 2 papers: Collins GL 10-11 T1 Q8; Exam Coach GL Q29. Both use fractional symbols, which is where the difficulty sits.

question_types.name: Venn and Carroll diagrams
question_types.evidence: 2 papers + the project's own paper (stats.venn): Collins CEM devotes a whole timed test - 5 questions on one 3-set Venn - to a skill with no home; Exam Coach GL also carries a Venn figure.

subtopics.target_rationale: gains 3 types; ran at 17.5% (Exam Coach GL) and 24% (ISEB) against a 6.5% target

axes._note: Statistics questions are a grid, not a list. File the axis that carries the difficulty as `question_type` and record the other in `also_tests`. A question with no representation (a plain list of numbers) has only an operation.

subtopics.name: Word Problems & Multi-Step Reasoning

question_types.name: Multi-step problems: adding and subtracting through
question_types.evidence: 2 papers: ISEB (6 of its 11 catch-all questions were accumulation chains); Exam Coach CEM.

question_types.name: Multi-step problems: needing a rate, product or scaling
question_types.evidence: 2 papers: ISEB (5 of 11 needed a multiplication or rate first); Exam Coach CEM.

subtopics.target_rationale: gains a type from the split; ran at 22-24% in two papers
